- Model consistently overestimates prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative (e.g., -1.00) — apply downward correction of 5–15% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is negative and prices are trending downward, model tends to ignore the trend and forecasts higher — reduce forecast by 3–8% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -1.00 → 1.00), model often overreacts with a sharp upward bias — cap forecast at 10–15% below recent peak or adjust to mean of last 5–7 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after 3–5 consecutive high forecasts, true values often dip — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility — use 10–15 day moving average or 30-day smoothed trend as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment is negative and true price drops sharply, model often fails to recognize the drop — apply lag correction: if true price drops >10% from 3-day average, reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5 days.
- Avoid forecasting above 10% above recent 7-day high unless sentiment is strongly positive (1.00) — cap forecast at 10% below recent peak if sentiment is negative.
